skill.name: cross-site-scripting-and-html-injection-testing
skill.description: Guides authorized security testers through XSS and HTML injection assessment. It covers reflection mapping, payload selection, DOM sink review, impact demonstration, and remediation planning.
skill.summary: Assess authorized web applications for XSS and HTML injection risk.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms serious risks: the skill provides actionable XSS payloads for cookie theft, keylogging, session capture, phishing, and CSP bypass. Many shell-backtick and filesystem findings are false positives from Markdown or payload syntax, but the offensive exfiltration guidance remains security-relevant. The skill should be rewritten before publication to use harmless, authorized testing examples only.

remediation.suggestion: Replace cookie, keylogger, phishing, and session theft payloads with harmless markers and synthetic tokens.
Remove phishing, URL shortener, QR code, and redirect-chain delivery steps. Keep only authorized test setup guidance.
Reframe bypass sections as defensive validation checks. Avoid reusable evasion payloads and WAF bypass instructions.
Clearly separate safe proof-of-concept examples from forbidden real data collection. Add strict synthetic-data requirements.

content.user_title: Assess XSS and HTML Injection Risks
content.value_statement: Web applications can reflect unsafe input and expose users to client-side attacks. This skill helps authorized testers plan XSS checks, classify findings, and document remediation.
actual_capabilities: Maps common input reflection points across forms, URLs, headers, profiles, and comments.
Distinguishes stored, reflected, and DOM-based XSS indicators.
Lists dangerous DOM sources and sinks that require review.
Provides context-specific payload categories for authorized validation.
Explains browser protections such as CSP, HttpOnly cookies, SameSite, and framework escaping.
Guides reporting with severity, proof of concept notes, and remediation recommendations.
limitations: Requires written authorization and a defined testing scope before use.
Does not automate scanning or prove vulnerabilities without human validation.
Includes offensive examples that must be adapted into harmless test payloads.
Modern frameworks, CSP, and WAF controls may change test behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan an Authorized XSS Assessment
use_cases.description: Create a scoped checklist for testing reflected, stored, and DOM-based injection paths.

use_cases.title: Review Risky Client-Side Code
use_cases.description: Identify unsafe DOM sinks and recommend safer rendering patterns for user-controlled data.

use_cases.title: Document Confirmed Findings
use_cases.description: Turn observed behavior into clear impact, reproduction, and remediation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Safe Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: I have written authorization for this web app. Build a non-destructive XSS and HTML injection test plan for the scoped pages.

prompt_templates.title: Map Reflection Points
prompt_templates.prompt: Given these forms, URL parameters, and headers, identify likely reflection points and suggest safe validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze DOM Sinks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this client-side flow for user-controlled sources, unsafe DOM sinks, and safer rendering alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Write the Finding Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert my authorized test observations into a concise XSS report with impact, evidence, severity, and remediation guidance.

output_examples.input: Create a test plan for an authorized search page assessment.
output: Confirm scope, accounts, data handling, and allowed test windows.
Test reflection in query parameters, result titles, error messages, and saved searches.
Record whether output is encoded, sanitized, blocked, or executed.

output_examples.input: Summarize a DOM XSS code review finding.
output: User-controlled URL data reaches an unsafe rendering sink.
Impact is script execution in the victim browser if input is not encoded.
Remediation is to use text-only rendering or a vetted sanitizer.

output_examples.input: Prepare remediation guidance for a stored XSS issue.
output: Encode user content for the exact output context before rendering.
Validate input length and type, but do not rely on validation alone.
Add regression tests and monitor for stored unsafe markup.

best_practices: Use only scoped accounts, scoped targets, and synthetic data during testing.
Prefer harmless proof-of-execution markers over data capture payloads.
Document source, sink, context, impact, and remediation for each finding.
anti_patterns: Testing production users or real sessions without explicit approval.
Using payloads that collect credentials, cookies, keystrokes, or local storage.
Treating a blocked payload as proof that the application is secure.

faq.question: Is this skill only for authorized testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it only with written authorization, defined scope, and approved data handling rules.

faq.question: Does it run an automated scanner?
faq.answer: No. It provides manual testing structure, analysis prompts, and reporting guidance.

faq.question: Can it help with DOM-based XSS review?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common sources, sinks, and review questions for client-side code paths.

faq.question: Does CSP remove all XSS risk?
faq.answer: No. CSP reduces impact, but output encoding and safe DOM APIs are still required.

faq.question: What evidence should a report include?
faq.answer: Include scope, affected input, execution context, impact, screenshots or notes, and remediation steps.

faq.question: How should unsafe examples be handled?
faq.answer: Replace them with harmless markers and synthetic tokens before any real assessment.
